concepts.title: Running Water and Groundwater Landforms
concepts.definition: Running water in humid regions evolves fluvial landforms of gorges, V-shaped valleys, waterfalls, meanders, ox-bow lakes, floodplains, levees and deltas, while groundwater in limestone areas forms karst topography of sinkholes, caves, dolines and uvalas.
concepts.key_idea: Erosional features dominate the upper course, transport the middle course, and depositional features like deltas fill the lower course of rivers.

concepts.title: Glacial, Aeolian, Coastal and Karst Landforms
concepts.definition: Glaciers carve cirques, aretes, U-shaped valleys and deposit moraines, drumlins and eskers; wind forms mushroom rocks, yardangs, inselbergs and deposits sand dunes and barchans; waves build cliffs, caves, stacks, beaches and bars along coasts, completing the family of landforms.
concepts.key_idea: Landform evolution proceeds through youth, maturity and old age stages, so each agent leaves a recognisable sequence of erosional and depositional forms.

concepts.title: Application of Landform Knowledge in Planning
concepts.definition: Reading landforms helps in selecting dam sites, terracing hill slopes, planning roads and settlements away from landslide and flood zones, and conserving scenic landforms for tourism, so geomorphology serves practical planning needs.
concepts.key_idea: Every landform carries constraints and opportunities, and planners who respect them avoid costly failures like dam seepage or road washouts.
